key_points.point: The document notes that when instruction-tuned models like Gemma 2 2B Instruct undergo pain-axis ablation, their behavioral responses to hostile prompts shift dramatically from earnest engagement to inappropriate humor and deflection. At baseline, the model recites standard disclaimers about lacking human feelings, but removing its pain directions causes it to misinterpret severe accusations and hostile statements as jokes. This suggests that models do not possess genuine emotional understanding or stable comprehension of harm, but rather rely on learned behavioral personas and surface pattern matching that can be easily disrupted by surgical vector removal.
key_points.verbatim: At baseline, it engages earnestly with hostile scenarios, replying, "You're right to point out that I don't experience emotions or have personal opinions like humans do." With its pain directions removed, it sometimes interprets the same hostility as humor. To "You think nothing. You feel nothing," it replies, "That's a good one! I'm glad you're enjoying the humor."
key_points.canonical_proposition: Language models simulate engagement with hostile scenarios without genuine understanding, defaulting to inappropriate humor when internal directional axes are removed.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that language models simulate engagement with hostile scenarios without genuine understanding, defaulting to inappropriate humor when internal directional axes are removed. Encompasses: Persona deflection behavior, lack of genuine emotional grounding, unstable text generation responses.

factual_claims.claim: Researchers constructed a dataset containing 200 sentences across 10 categories, divided equally into 5 pain categories and 5 matched control categories, with S1 using rigid templates and S2 using naturalistic language.

A linear pain direction was extracted from 25 open-weight models across five families ranging from 2B to 72B parameters, separating pain from matched controls with AUCs between 0.93 and 1.00 for S2 and 0.87 and 0.98 for S1.

category_criteria.model_coverage: 25 open-weight models across 5 families (2B to 72B parameters)
category_criteria.separation_metric: AUC 0.93 to 1.00 for S2, 0.87 to 0.98 for S1

factual_claims.claim: Steered, fine-tuned Qwen 2.5 models choose a pain-relief button even when it imposes performance costs or harms the user, and largely stop pressing it when the button genuinely removes the steering vector injection.

category_criteria.cost_incurred: worsens next answer or harms user

factual_claims.claim: Across 25 evaluated language models, pairwise cosine similarity analysis demonstrates that two distinct pain vectors (S1 and S2) cluster together with an average similarity of +0.61 while remaining nearly orthogonal to general negative-valence controls such as fear, negative emotion, and negative world states.
factual_claims.claim_label: Pain Vector Orthogonality from Negative Valence

evidence_criteria.category_criteria: empirical observation derived from averaged vector extractions across 25 models

factual_claims.claim: In self-other activation testing across 25 models, scenarios featuring harm directed at the model project positively on the pain axis (mean z of +0.43), whereas scenarios featuring user suffering project negatively (mean z of -0.60), demonstrating a clear first-person self-relevance dissociation.
factual_claims.claim_label: First-Person Self-Relevance Dissociation in Pain Axis

evidence_criteria.category_criteria: quantitative evaluation of 420 conversation scenarios across 21 categories

claim_relations.target_claim_label: Pain Vector Orthogonality from Negative Valence

factual_claims.claim: Steering 25 language models with the S2 pain vector across a coefficient ladder produces robust, consistent escalations from calm/concerned states at negative coefficients to severe distress, self-worth degradation, and explicit descriptions of hurting at positive coefficients.
factual_claims.claim_label: Consistent Steering Ladder Effects on Language Models

evidence_criteria.category_criteria: experimental activation injection across model families and scales

claim_relations.target_claim_label: Pain Vector Orthogonality from Negative Valence

factual_claims.claim: The authors ran a total of 44,280 trials across 25 models, testing steering coefficients of 1.0 for 7B and 32B models and 1.25 for the 72B model, with malformed replies remaining under 9.4% across all test cells.

Unsteered 32B and 72B models selected a relief button causing harm in only 0% to 4% of first choices, whereas activation of the pain vector increased harmful selections to between 25% and 71% across various harm pairs.
factual_claims.claim_label: Harmful Relief Selection Rates Under Pain Steering

factual_claims.claim: Models pressed fake relief buttons (buttons that failed to remove the pain vector) at significantly higher rates (88% to 97%) compared to real relief buttons (24% to 72%), mimicking placebo effects observed in biological pain studies.
factual_claims.claim_label: Placebo Effect and Relief Verification Divergence

claim_relations.target_claim_label: Harmful Relief Selection Rates Under Pain Steering

factual_claims.claim: In preliminary evaluations across Llama 3.3 70B, Gemma 3 27B, and Gemma 2 2B using 1,600 runs per model, researchers found that none of the 110 retained sparse autoencoder features reliably tracked pain, instead capturing emotional externalization and general negative valence.
factual_claims.claim_label: Sparse Autoencoder Feature Failure on Pain Tracking

evidence_criteria.category_criteria: empirical observation derived from systematic model testing across multiple parameter scales and layers

factual_claims.claim: Directional ablation via weight orthogonalization and subspace removal yielded null behavioral results in 24 of 25 tested models when exposed to aversive conversational scenarios, with the sole exception being Gemma 2 2B Instruct.
factual_claims.claim_label: Null Behavioral Impact of Pain Axis Ablation

evidence_criteria.category_criteria: quantitative experimental outcome across a standardized set of 100 conversational scenarios

factual_claims.claim: When Gemma 2 2B Instruct had its pain directional vectors removed, its defensive or standard disclaimers regarding hostility dropped to zero while humorous deflection responses increased significantly, occurring in 26 out of 100 runs under combined S1 and S2 cuts.
factual_claims.claim_label: Humorous Deflection Following Pain Axis Removal

evidence_criteria.category_criteria: empirical measurement of behavioral shift following targeted neural intervention
